test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 10 Jul, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

After your insistence, / my sister / checked / a mailbox again.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"a mailbox again" **should be corrected to** "the mailbox again" **to make the sentence** grammatically correct.**
 
• The word** "a" **suggests **any mailbox**, whereas **"the" specifies a particular mailbox that is already known to the speaker and listener.**
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase should be **"the mailbox again".**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *After your insistence, my sister checked** the mailbox **again*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In English grammar, definite and indefinite articles** ("the" and "a" or "an") **are used to indicate specificity or generality respectively.
 
• **"The"** is used when referring to something specific or previously mentioned.
 
• **"A"** or "an" is used when referring to something in a general sense or when it is mentioned for the first time.
